title: Spec-driven tool orchestration kickoff with Auric Systems
summary: Intro + live API + Console demo showing spec-driven JSON mode, safe tool calling and runtime fallbacks. Discussed VPC/private options, SOC2/KMS concerns, pilot scope and next steps for a 6-week pilot with a latency/cost eval.
topics: Guardrails: policy-driven fallbacks and safe tool execution
Private deployment / VPC / KMS and compliance
transcript:
Header:
- Date: 2027-12-14
- Start: 16:00 UTC
- Duration: ~54 minutes
- Attendees: Jamie Ortiz; Samir Patel; Alejandra Cruz; Ryan Holt; Leah Kim; Darren Cho; Priya Menon; Tom Rivera

Auto-summary (auto): Quick demo of JSON-mode tool calling, runtime fallbacks, and a pilot ask.

[00:00:04] Jamie Ortiz: okay everyone thanks for joining, i'm jamie from Redwood Inference, i'm the AE on the account, um we'll do quick intros and then hand to samir for the deep dive.
[00:00:12] Leah Kim: hey thanks jamie, leah here, head of platform at auric systems. we pulled in darren and priya. quick note we have a hard security review next month so want to make sure those bits are clear.
[00:00:20] Darren Cho: yeah i'm darren ml eng, mostly interested in the tool invocation and typed outputs, like can it guarantee a schema?
[00:00:24] Priya Menon: priya security, questions around audit logs, kms, and whether the console leaks data — basically everything will be audited.
[00:00:30] Samir Patel: perfect, good to know. i'll try to show the console in a way that highlights audit trails and the private options. Alejandra will also show the optimize tab and batching suggestions.
[00:01:05] Jamie Ortiz: quick agenda, one demo of the API typed-output mode, then console live: schema registry, tool sandbox and a fallback sim, and finally optimize recommendations + pilot ask.
[00:01:30] Tom Rivera: timeline wise we are evaluating now, pilot decision in 2 weeks ideally.

[00:02:10] Samir Patel: alright jumping into the API — so two modes we show a json-mode where you declare a contract, e.g. {"user_intent": "string", "entities": [ {"type":"string","text":"string"} ] } and the runtime enforces validation and returns structured responses or explicit parse errors. if it can't satisfy the schema within token budget we have a fallback policy to call a lighter model or to return partial fields with confidence metadata.
[00:03:05] Darren Cho: when you say enforce validation, is that pre- or post-generation? how do you guard against hallucinated fields that match schema shapes?
[00:03:18] Samir Patel: good question — it's a combo. runtime checks the output and runs a validator; if the validator fails we trigger a corrective prompt or a function/tool call to a deterministic extractor, depending on policy. the idea is to prefer deterministic post-processing for high-stakes fields. note though the transcription sometimes calls KV cache as 'k v cash' in logs, sorry for the voice, um yeah.
[00:04:00] Speaker 1: (muffled) can you show the console example?
[00:04:10] Alejandra Cruz: sure, switching to the console — alright i'm opening the model catalog, we picked a customer open model for demo but you can pin a quantized variant. here is the schema registry, you can upload an OpenAPI-like json schema or craft a simple contract inline. i'll create a short schema for an invoice parsing flow.
[00:05:05] Alejandra Cruz: now the tool sandbox, this is where you can register external functions (e.g. ledger.lookup, ticket.create). you can provide a dry-run mode where we simulate tool calls and show a detailed audit trail. note that the console shows the call stack and the inputs/outputs, which are redacted if you enable PII masking.
[00:05:46] Priya Menon: how is masking implemented? do you store raw payloads anywhere?
[00:05:53] Alejandra Cruz: by default we store minimal tokens for debugging, you can enable full PII stripping which hashes sensitive fields before storage; for private deployments you can opt out and ship logs to your own S3 behind your KMS.
[00:06:12] Tom Rivera: and KMS — do you support customer-managed keys (CMK)?
[00:06:17] Samir Patel: yes, CMK via the cloud KMS integration and HSM-based keys are supported for our Private offering. our hosted plan uses envelope encryption but you can request dedicated key configurations.
[00:06:34] Leah Kim: okay cool. can you simulate a failure and show fallback to a cheaper model? we want graceful degradation.
[00:06:42] Samir Patel: yeah i'll do a live sim — i'll intentionally set a tight token window and force a validation failure, then show fallback policy — ok running.
[00:07:05] [00:07:20] Samir Patel: so the initial call returned a validation error: "missing required field: customer_id". the runtime policy chose fallback=try-extractor then fallback=model-light. first extractor call pulled customer_id from a short index lookup tool; the console shows the replay with timestamps and approximate latency per step.
[00:07:50] Darren Cho: that extractor is deterministic? is it hosted on your infra or ours?
[00:07:56] Samir Patel: you can host it yourself behind our function gateway or run it as a Redwood managed microservice in the Private topology. we recommend hosting PII-sensitive extractors on your side for compliance.

[00:09:10] Jamie Ortiz: switching topics — optimize tab. this is where we show suggestions: batching window vs latency curves, quantization recommendation (int4 vs int8), and prefix caching heuristics.
[00:09:32] Alejandra Cruz: for your workload pattern (long chat prompts + few API calls), we suggested small KV cache with persistent prefix for session-level context and 50ms batching target. the optimizer estimated a 28% token-cost reduction with the suggested params.
[00:10:05] Leah Kim: curious about latency impact — 50ms batching sounds okay but our SLO is 200ms p95; how does batching affect tail latencies?
[00:10:16] Alejandra Cruz: the optimizer models tails — for tight SLOs we favor caching over batching. caching reduces token generation per request and preserves latency; batching can reduce cost but increases median slightly. you can configure a routing policy that prioritizes low-latency region or dedicated pool for critical routes.
[00:11:00] Darren Cho: any benchmarks you can share for similar workloads?
[00:11:06] Jamie Ortiz: we'll send a benchmark spreadsheet after the call — we have examples from retail invoice parsing and a chat app — i'll attach those.
[00:11:15] Tom Rivera: competitors? who do we benchmark against?
[00:11:20] Jamie Ortiz: typically we see teams comparing with OpenAI for hosted convenience, Anthropic for safety-first models, and Lambda Labs or self-hosted Triton stacks for on-prem performance.

[00:12:00] Priya Menon: back to security: do you provide SOC 2 attestation and detailed audit logs per token?
[00:12:06] Samir Patel: yes we have SOC 2 Type II for hosted customers, and you get audit logs that include model variant, route, redaction state, and function calls. for Private customers we provide the audit schema and help integrate with your SIEM.
[00:12:30] Leah Kim: can the audit show who triggered a function call? we need user-level traceability.
[00:12:36] Alejandra Cruz: yep each request is tagged with user_id and token-level metadata when available; for privacy you can limit that at ingestion.

[00:13:20] [00:13:20] Samir Patel: demo — now i'll create a simple schema-bound tool flow: user asks for invoice status, model returns JSON with invoice_id, status, confidence. then the runtime calls ledger.lookup with invoice_id and emits a typed response.
[00:13:50] [00:14:05] Samir Patel: running live — okay transcript: the model returned a structured payload but with an extra field 'total_amtt' (typo). our validator flagged it as unknown field, policy is 'reject-unknown' so the pipeline invoked a sanitizer step that mapped 'total_amtt' -> 'total_amount' using a deterministic mapping table. the console shows that mapping step and the operator who configured it.
[00:14:40] Darren Cho: nice. how do you author those sanitizer mappings? is there a UI?
[00:14:46] Alejandra Cruz: yep there's a mapping editor in the console and you can store rules per schema version. rules support regex and normalization functions.

[00:15:30] Leah Kim: do you support function/tool calling chaining? like call A then B only if A returns X?
[00:15:36] Samir Patel: yes conditional orchestration is supported in the route policy. you can express it in the console or via a declarative yaml; we also support canary policies so you can test changes on a small percent of traffic.

[00:16:55] Tom Rivera: what's the network topology for Private — do you require a VPN or peered VPC? latency wise we worry about a hop to your control plane.
[00:17:04] Jamie Ortiz: for Private we offer two modes — VPC peering with a private control plane or an on-prem package where control plane runs inside your data center. peering keeps control plane traffic in the backbone; the data plane stays in your network for guaranteed residency.
[00:17:25] Priya Menon: and the console? if we pick peering do engineers access the console over our VPN?
[00:17:30] Alejandra Cruz: yes console endpoints can be restricted to your corporate IPs or via SAML SSO. we integrate with Okta, Azure AD, and generic SAML providers.

[00:18:20] [00:18:20] Samir Patel: i want to show the 'simulate & assert' runner — this is where you run a recall suite of prompts against new model variants and your schema set. you can author tests, assert shapes, and fail builds if regression occurs. good for preventing quiet regressions in open model updates.
[00:18:50] Darren Cho: will that fail CI? can it integrate with our github actions?
[00:18:55] Alejandra Cruz: yes you can export results as JSON and there's a CLI client that calls the simulate API; many teams run it in CI and gate deploys.

[00:20:10] Leah Kim: ok let's talk pilot: our constraints — SOC2 + KMS, 3rd party audit, 100k tokens/day initial, p95 latency target 200ms, must run in our VPC. timeline 6 weeks to production for a small flow.
[00:20:30] Jamie Ortiz: sounds doable — proposed pilot: 6 weeks, start with invoice parsing flow, dedicated pilot environment (private control plane + peered data plane), weekly checkpoints, and a mid-pilot benchmark at week 3. deliverables: runbook, audit docs, cost estimates, and final performance report.
[00:21:05] Tom Rivera: pricing ballpark for dedicated pilot?
[00:21:10] Jamie Ortiz: i'll send a pilot quote but rough numbers: pilot reserved capacity monthly pro-rated; for 100k tokens/day with a mixed model we estimate X for infra + Y for support — i'll follow up in email with a detailed breakdown.

[00:22:00] [00:22:00] Samir Patel: back to the demo — one more safety bit: we have runtime policy guards that prevent tool calls to sensitive functions unless a rule allows it. e.g. only requests with auth_role=ops can call ledger.delete. policies are enforced at the gateway.
[00:22:30] Priya Menon: can we see an audit of that enforcement?
[00:22:36] Alejandra Cruz: yep here's a log excerpt (redacted for demo) showing deny events and who attempted the call. it's searchable in the console.

[00:23:20] Darren Cho: just a technical nit — when you do quantization suggestions, do you produce per-model accuracy deltas? i.e. int4 vs float16 tradeoffs?
[00:23:30] Alejandra Cruz: the optimizer provides expected quality deltas from our benchmark traces; for critical fields you can pin post-eval tests to ensure the quantized model meets your thresholds.

[00:24:10] [00:24:10] Jamie Ortiz: okay we're approaching the middle of the call — any blockers or immediate concerns?
[00:24:20] Leah Kim: main blocker is legal/3rd party audit — we need the SOC2 report, encryption details, and a sample DPA.
[00:24:30] Jamie Ortiz: noted — we'll attach SOC2, DPA template, and security whitepaper.

[00:25:05] Samir Patel: quick show of the telemetry panels — here's route-level p95, token-cost per request, and function-call rate. you can set alerts on anomalies and on quality regression tied to eval prompt sets.
[00:25:40] Tom Rivera: can alerts trigger automated fallbacks? we want to failover to a safe model when precision drops below threshold.
[00:25:47] Samir Patel: yes you can configure alert-based routing that switches the route to a conservative model or enables extra validation steps.

[00:27:00] Darren Cho: what's the on-call support SLA during pilot?
[00:27:05] Jamie Ortiz: pilot includes standard support; we can add a dedicated SE rotation for enterprise pilots at the add-on level — i'll quote that in the pricing doc.

[00:28:10] [00:28:10] Alejandra Cruz: demoing one more feature — response annotations: the model can emit field-level confidence and provenance; provenance can show whether a field came from the model, an extractor, or a cached prefix.
[00:28:40] Leah Kim: provenance would be helpful for compliance so we can attribute where data came from.

[00:29:20] Samir Patel: quick Q&A — Darren: can we run a subset of workloads on your hosted infra to speed up evaluation?
[00:29:30] Jamie Ortiz: yes hybrid pilots are possible — you can run low-risk routes on hosted and PII-sensitive ones in your VPC.

[00:30:05] [00:30:05] Priya Menon: legal will want a list of subprocessors and data residency options.
[00:30:12] Jamie Ortiz: we'll include subprocessors and region options in the follow-up package.

[00:31:00] Tom Rivera: how do version rollouts work? if a model update causes a regression we need instant rollback.
[00:31:06] Alejandra Cruz: our rollout system supports automatic rollback on regression triggers and manual canaries. you can set percent traffic, evaluate, and abort automatically if key eval tests fail.

[00:32:20] Darren Cho: performance testing — can we bring our own test harness?
[00:32:25] Samir Patel: absolutely, we support the open load clients and you can run tests against the dedicated endpoints; we'll also provide sample configs.

[00:33:10] Leah Kim: ok i'm trying to summarize the success criteria: pass security review (SOC2 + DPA), meet p95 latency 200ms, and maintain >95% schema-pass for invoice fields.
[00:33:24] Jamie Ortiz: that's a good set — we'll map those into the pilot runbook.

[00:34:00] [00:34:00] Samir Patel: minor hiccup in the demo — console replay got a transient 503 for a moment, likely because i had aggressive rate-limiting in the sandbox, apologies.
[00:34:18] Speaker 1: (laughs) real world demo.

[00:35:05] Alejandra Cruz: closing the demo — any final product questions?
[00:35:12] Darren Cho: one more: how strict is the schema evolution story — can we run multiple schema versions in parallel?
[00:35:20] Samir Patel: yes we support schema versions and per-route version pinning; traffic can be split between versions for gradual migration.

[00:36:00] Leah Kim: ok let's go into logistics — next steps and owners.
[00:36:10] Jamie Ortiz: propose next steps: 1) Jamie to send pilot quote + benchmark spreadsheet + SOC2 + DPA (by 2027-12-17); 2) Auric to share sample invoice dataset (anonymized) and success metrics (by 2027-12-20); 3) schedule kickoff for week of 2027-12-27.
[00:36:45] Priya Menon: legal will need to review the DPA quickly, can you include subprocessors?
[00:36:52] Jamie Ortiz: yes will include subprocessors.

[00:37:30] [00:37:30] Tom Rivera: is there a cost to the pilot itself? we expect some infra charges.
[00:37:36] Jamie Ortiz: pilot infra is pro-rated; there is also a professional services estimate if you want dedicated support. i'll include both a minimal and an accelerated plan.

[00:38:50] Darren Cho: can we run an A/B test where 10% of traffic uses the sanitizer mapping and 90% uses raw model to compare precision?
[00:38:58] Samir Patel: yes, traffic-splitting is built into rollouts.

[00:40:10] Leah Kim: ok thanks — any blockers from our side? we need to confirm legal and share the dataset.
[00:40:18] Priya Menon: i'll coordinate legal and security, expect questions on the DPA and subprocessors.

[00:41:00] [00:41:00] Jamie Ortiz: great, i'll follow up with the email and attach the docs. before we close any final tech asks?
[00:41:12] Darren Cho: maybe one: can you run an initial benchmark with our sample dataset and provide p95 estimates?
[00:41:20] Jamie Ortiz: yes we'll run a bench as part of the pilot prep and share numbers in the week-1 kickoff.

[00:43:00] Alejandra Cruz: one more note on safety: we also support offline review queues where human ops can approve high-risk actions before tool execution.
[00:43:12] Leah Kim: that's good to know.

[00:44:00] [00:44:00] Jamie Ortiz: ok wrapping up — thanks everyone for your time. we'll send the follow-up package with pilot quote and security artifacts by friday (2027-12-17). leave any questions on the thread.
[00:44:20] Tom Rivera: thanks jamie, thanks team.
[00:44:22] Samir Patel: thanks all.
[00:44:25] Transcript end.

Auric Systems (Leah Kim) - Share anonymized invoice dataset and success metrics - 2027-12-20
